hanani_1379.name: Hanani
hanani_1379.who: A seer in Judah who rebuked King Asa and was the father of the prophet Jehu.
key: His son Jehu brought the Lord's word of judgment against King Baasha of Israel (1 Kings 16).
Hanani rebuked King Asa for relying on the king of Syria instead of the Lord (2 Chronicles 16).
Asa grew angry at Hanani and put him in the stocks in prison (2 Chronicles 16).
His son Jehu later rebuked King Jehoshaphat for helping Ahab (2 Chronicles 19).

haran_1407.name: Haran
haran_1407.who: A son of Terah, brother of Abram and Nahor, and father of Lot, Milcah, and Iscah.
key: Haran was born to Terah, along with his brothers Abram and Nahor (Genesis 11).
He fathered Lot, as well as daughters Milcah and Iscah (Genesis 11).
He died in Ur of the Chaldeans while his father Terah was still living (Genesis 11).
His daughter Milcah married his brother Nahor, and Terah took Lot toward Canaan (Genesis 11).

harim_1416.name: Harim
harim_1416.who: A priest in David's time whose family became the third of the priestly divisions and later returned from exile.
key: Harim's family received the third lot among the priestly divisions under David (1 Chronicles 24).
More than a thousand priests descended from Harim returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
Several priests of Harim's line were listed among those who had married foreign wives (Ezra 10).
Nehemiah's register again records the priestly family of Harim among the returned exiles (Nehemiah 7).

helon_1486.name: Helon
helon_1486.who: A man of Zebulun whose son Eliab led the tribe during Israel's wilderness journey.
key: His son Eliab was named to help Moses take the census for Zebulun (Numbers 1).
Eliab son of Helon led Zebulun's camp on the east side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).
Eliab brought Zebulun's offering on the third day of the altar's dedication (Numbers 7).
Eliab commanded Zebulun's company when Israel set out from Sinai (Numbers 10).

hepher_1496.name: Hepher
hepher_1496.who: A son of Gilead in the tribe of Manasseh and the grandfather of Zelophehad's five daughters.
key: Hepher was a son of Gilead and head of the Hepherite clan of Manasseh (Numbers 26).
His son Zelophehad had no sons, only five daughters (Numbers 26).
Zelophehad's daughters asked Moses for an inheritance, and the Lord granted it (Numbers 27).
Hepher's clan received its portion within Manasseh's allotment of land (Joshua 17).

hezron_1519.name: Hezron
hezron_1519.who: A son of Reuben and the founder of the Hezronite clan in the tribe of Reuben.
key: Hezron went down to Egypt with Jacob's family as one of Reuben's sons (Genesis 46).
He is listed among the heads of the fathers' houses of Reuben (Exodus 6).
His descendants formed the clan of the Hezronites at the second census (Numbers 26).
Chronicles again lists him among the sons of Reuben, Israel's firstborn (1 Chronicles 5).

hilkiah_1523.name: Hilkiah
hilkiah_1523.who: The father of Eliakim, who was over the royal household under King Hezekiah of Judah.
key: His son Eliakim went out to meet the Assyrian field commander at Jerusalem (2 Kings 18).
Isaiah prophesied that God would call Eliakim son of Hilkiah to replace Shebna (Isaiah 22).
Eliakim reported the Assyrian commander's threats to Hezekiah with torn clothes (Isaiah 36).

hiram_1533.name: Hiram
hiram_1533.who: A skilled bronze worker from Tyre who made the bronze pillars and furnishings for Solomon's temple.
key: Solomon brought Hiram from Tyre; his mother was a widow of the tribe of Naphtali (1 Kings 7).
He cast the two bronze pillars, Jachin and Boaz, for the temple porch (1 Kings 7).
He made the bronze sea, the stands, the basins, and other temple vessels (1 Kings 7).
He finished the work he did for King Solomon on the house of God (2 Chronicles 4).

hophni_1550.name: Hophni
hophni_1550.who: A son of the priest Eli who served at Shiloh and treated the Lord's offerings with contempt.
key: Hophni and his brother Phinehas served as priests of the Lord at Shiloh (1 Samuel 1).
They abused the sacrifices and ignored their father's warnings (1 Samuel 2).
A man of God foretold that both brothers would die on the same day (1 Samuel 2).
Hophni was killed by the Philistines in the battle where the ark was captured (1 Samuel 4).

immer_599.name: Immer
immer_599.who: A priest whose family became the sixteenth priestly division and returned from exile in Babylon.
key: Immer's family drew the sixteenth lot among the priestly divisions under David (1 Chronicles 24).
More than a thousand priests of Immer's line returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
Two of his descendants, Hanani and Zebadiah, had married foreign wives (Ezra 10).
Pashhur son of Immer, chief officer in the temple, beat Jeremiah and put him in stocks (Jeremiah 20).

james_718.name: James
james_718.who: The son of Alphaeus and one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus.
key: Jesus named James son of Alphaeus among the twelve apostles he sent out (Matthew 10).
Mark lists him among the Twelve appointed to preach and cast out demons (Mark 3).
Luke names him among the apostles Jesus chose after a night of prayer (Luke 6).
He was with the apostles praying in the upper room after Jesus' ascension (Acts 1).

jason_742.name: Jason
jason_742.who: A believer in Thessalonica who hosted Paul and Silas and was dragged before the city authorities.
key: A mob attacked Jason's house while searching for Paul and Silas (Acts 17).
They dragged Jason before the city authorities, accusing him of harboring the missionaries (Acts 17).
The authorities released Jason and the others after taking money as security (Acts 17).
Paul's letter to Rome includes greetings from a Jason, one of his kinsmen (Romans 16).

jehu_816.name: Jehu
jehu_816.who: A prophet, son of Hanani the seer, who announced judgment on King Baasha and rebuked King Jehoshaphat.
key: Jehu announced that the Lord would sweep away Baasha's house for his sins (1 Kings 16).
Zimri destroyed Baasha's whole house, fulfilling the word spoken through Jehu (1 Kings 16).
He rebuked Jehoshaphat for helping wicked Ahab, while noting good in him (2 Chronicles 19).
He wrote a record of Jehoshaphat's acts, included in the Book of the Kings of Israel (2 Chronicles 20).

joses_1721.name: Joses
joses_1721.who: One of the brothers of Jesus, named with James, Simon, and Judas by the people of Nazareth.
key: The people of Nazareth named Joses among Jesus' brothers when they took offense at him (Matthew 13).
Mark also lists Joses with James, Judas, and Simon as brothers of Jesus (Mark 6).

kenaz_1778.name: Kenaz
kenaz_1778.who: A man of Judah, father of Othniel, Israel's first judge, and of Seraiah.
key: His son Othniel captured Debir and received Caleb's daughter Achsah as his wife (Joshua 15).
Judges again records Othniel son of Kenaz taking Debir (Judges 1).
The Lord raised up Othniel son of Kenaz to deliver Israel from Cushan-rishathaim (Judges 3).
Chronicles lists Othniel and Seraiah as the sons of Kenaz (1 Chronicles 4).

lebbaeus_1815.name: Thaddaeus
lebbaeus_1815.who: One of the twelve apostles, called Thaddaeus in Matthew and Mark and Judas son of James in Luke and Acts.
key: Jesus named Thaddaeus among the twelve apostles he sent out (Matthew 10).
Luke lists this apostle as Judas son of James, distinct from Judas Iscariot (Luke 6).
At the Last Supper he asked why Jesus would reveal himself to them and not the world (John 14).
He joined the other apostles in prayer in the upper room after the ascension (Acts 1).

lotan_1831.name: Lotan
lotan_1831.who: A son of Seir the Horite and one of the Horite chiefs in the land of Seir.
key: Lotan is listed among the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land (Genesis 36).
His sons were Hori and Hemam, and his sister was Timna (Genesis 36).
He was one of the chiefs of the Horites in the land of Seir (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats his family line among the descendants of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

magog_1882.name: Magog
magog_1882.who: A son of Japheth in the table of nations, whose name later designates a distant northern land and people.
key: Magog is listed among the sons of Japheth, son of Noah (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats his name among Japheth's descendants (1 Chronicles 1).
Ezekiel names Magog as the land of Gog, who would come against Israel (Ezekiel 38).
God declared he would send fire on Magog and make his name known (Ezekiel 39).
Revelation names Gog and Magog among nations Satan gathers for battle (Revelation 20).

mattithiah_1974.name: Mattithiah
mattithiah_1974.who: A Levite musician, son of Jeduthun, who played the lyre in worship before the ark under David.
key: Mattithiah was appointed among the Levites to play lyres when the ark was brought up (1 Chronicles 15).
He served under Asaph with harps and lyres before the ark of the Lord (1 Chronicles 16).
He was one of the sons of Jeduthun who prophesied with the lyre (1 Chronicles 25).
He received the fourteenth lot for service among the temple musicians (1 Chronicles 25).

meshelemiah_2013.name: Meshelemiah
meshelemiah_2013.who: A Korahite Levite, son of Kore, who headed a family of gatekeepers in David's time.
key: His son Zechariah was gatekeeper at the entrance of the tent of meeting (1 Chronicles 9).
Meshelemiah son of Kore was a Korahite gatekeeper with seven sons (1 Chronicles 26).
His sons and brothers numbered eighteen able men (1 Chronicles 26).
The lot for the east gate fell to him, there called Shelemiah (1 Chronicles 26).

michael_2068.name: Michael
michael_2068.who: An archangel, described as a chief prince who stands guard over God's people.
key: Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help against the prince of Persia (Daniel 10).
He is called the great prince who protects Daniel's people in a time of trouble (Daniel 12).
Jude says the archangel Michael disputed with the devil about the body of Moses (Jude 1).
Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon was thrown down (Revelation 12).

nathan_2152.name: Nathan
nathan_2152.who: A son of David and Bathsheba, born in Jerusalem, through whom Luke traces Jesus' genealogy.
key: Nathan was one of the sons born to David in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5).
Chronicles names him among four sons Bathsheba bore to David, including Solomon (1 Chronicles 3).
Zechariah foresees the family of the house of Nathan mourning by itself (Zechariah 12).
Luke traces Jesus' genealogy back through Nathan the son of David (Luke 3).

nebajoth_2164.name: Nebaioth
nebajoth_2164.who: The firstborn son of Ishmael, whose descendants became one of the twelve Ishmaelite tribes.
key: Nebaioth was the firstborn of Ishmael's twelve sons, each a tribal prince (Genesis 25).
Esau married Mahalath, Ishmael's daughter and the sister of Nebaioth (Genesis 28).
Basemath, another of Esau's wives, is also called Nebaioth's sister (Genesis 36).
Isaiah foresees the rams of Nebaioth accepted on God's altar (Isaiah 60).

nehemiah_2172.name: Nehemiah
nehemiah_2172.who: Son of Hacaliah, cupbearer to King Artaxerxes, who became governor of Judah and rebuilt Jerusalem's walls.
key: Hearing that Jerusalem's walls lay broken, Nehemiah wept, fasted, and prayed (Nehemiah 1).
King Artaxerxes granted his request and sent him to rebuild the city (Nehemiah 2).
Despite opposition, the wall was finished in fifty-two days (Nehemiah 6).
He stood with Ezra as the Law was read and explained to the people (Nehemiah 8).
Returning to Jerusalem, he corrected abuses in the temple, the Sabbath, and marriages (Nehemiah 13).

nethaneel_2188.name: Nethanel
nethaneel_2188.who: The son of Zuar and chief of the tribe of Issachar during the wilderness years.
key: Nethanel was appointed to help Moses take the census for Issachar (Numbers 1).
He led Issachar's camp on the east side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).
He presented Issachar's offering on the second day of the altar's dedication (Numbers 7).
He commanded Issachar's company when Israel set out from Sinai (Numbers 10).

nicodemus_2204.name: Nicodemus
nicodemus_2204.who: A Pharisee and ruler of the Jews who came to Jesus by night and later helped bury him.
key: Nicodemus came to Jesus by night, and Jesus taught him about being born again (John 3).
He urged the Pharisees not to condemn Jesus without first giving him a hearing (John 7).
With Joseph of Arimathea, he brought myrrh and aloes and buried Jesus' body (John 19).

nimshi_2207.name: Nimshi
nimshi_2207.who: The grandfather of King Jehu of Israel, who is often called Jehu son of Nimshi.
key: The Lord told Elijah to anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king over Israel (1 Kings 19).
Elisha sent a prophet to anoint Jehu, son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi (2 Kings 9).
The watchman recognized Jehu son of Nimshi by his furious driving (2 Kings 9).
God anointed Jehu son of Nimshi to destroy the house of Ahab (2 Chronicles 22).

ocran_2235.name: Ochran
ocran_2235.who: A man of Asher whose son Pagiel led the tribe during Israel's wilderness journey.
key: His son Pagiel was named to help Moses take the census for Asher (Numbers 1).
Pagiel son of Ochran led Asher's camp on the north side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).
Pagiel brought Asher's offering on the eleventh day of the altar's dedication (Numbers 7).
Pagiel commanded Asher's company when Israel set out from Sinai (Numbers 10).

pagiel_2264.name: Pagiel
pagiel_2264.who: The son of Ochran and chief of the tribe of Asher during the wilderness years.
key: Pagiel was appointed to help Moses take the census for Asher (Numbers 1).
He led Asher's camp on the north side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).
He presented Asher's offering on the eleventh day of the altar's dedication (Numbers 7).
He commanded Asher's company when Israel set out from Sinai (Numbers 10).

pallu_2325.name: Pallu
pallu_2325.who: A son of Reuben, founder of the Palluite clan and ancestor of Dathan and Abiram.
key: Pallu went down to Egypt with Jacob's family as one of Reuben's sons (Genesis 46).
He is listed among the heads of the fathers' houses of Reuben (Exodus 6).
His son Eliab was the father of Dathan and Abiram, who rebelled against Moses (Numbers 26).
Chronicles again lists him among the sons of Reuben (1 Chronicles 5).

pashur_2283.name: Pashhur
pashur_2283.who: A priest, son of Malchijah, whose large family of descendants returned from exile and served in Jerusalem.
key: Pashhur appears as an ancestor of Adaiah, a priest living in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9).
More than twelve hundred of Pashhur's descendants returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
Six priests descended from Pashhur had married foreign wives (Ezra 10).
Priests of Pashhur's line served in the house of God after the return (Nehemiah 11).

pedahzur_2291.name: Pedahzur
pedahzur_2291.who: A man of Manasseh whose son Gamaliel led the tribe during Israel's wilderness journey.
key: His son Gamaliel was named to help Moses take the census for Manasseh (Numbers 1).
Gamaliel son of Pedahzur led Manasseh's camp on the west side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).
Gamaliel brought Manasseh's offering on the eighth day of the altar's dedication (Numbers 7).
Gamaliel commanded Manasseh's company when Israel set out from Sinai (Numbers 10).

pharaoh_2330.name: Pharaoh
pharaoh_2330.who: The king of Egypt who enslaved the Israelites and ordered their newborn sons to be killed.
key: A new king who did not know Joseph enslaved Israel with hard labor (Exodus 1).
He ordered the Hebrew midwives to kill newborn boys, but they feared God (Exodus 1).
He commanded that every Hebrew son be thrown into the Nile (Exodus 1).
His daughter found the baby Moses in the river and raised him as her son (Exodus 2).
When Moses killed an Egyptian, Pharaoh sought to kill him, and Moses fled (Exodus 2).

pharaoh_2333.name: Pharaoh
pharaoh_2333.who: The king of Egypt in Hezekiah's day, whose help Judah sought against the Assyrians.
key: The Assyrian commander mocked trust in Pharaoh as leaning on a broken reed (2 Kings 18).
Isaiah declared that the wise counselors of Pharaoh gave foolish counsel (Isaiah 19).
Isaiah warned that seeking Pharaoh's protection would bring Judah shame (Isaiah 30).
The Assyrian commander repeated that Pharaoh fails all who rely on him (Isaiah 36).

rehum_2413.name: Rehum
rehum_2413.who: A leader among the exiles who returned from Babylon to Judah with Zerubbabel.
key: Rehum was among the leaders who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
A Rehum was among the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10).
A Rehum is also listed among those who came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12).

seraiah_2494.name: Seraiah
seraiah_2494.who: The chief priest of Judah when Jerusalem fell, executed by the king of Babylon at Riblah.
key: Nebuzaradan took Seraiah the chief priest captive when Jerusalem fell (2 Kings 25).
He was brought to the king of Babylon at Riblah and put to death (2 Kings 25).
Chronicles lists him as son of Azariah and father of Jehozadak, who went into exile (1 Chronicles 6).
Ezra the scribe traced his priestly descent through Seraiah back to Aaron (Ezra 7).

shallum_2519.name: Shallum
shallum_2519.who: A priest in Zadok's line and father of Hilkiah, the high priest in King Josiah's day.
key: Chronicles places Shallum between Zadok and Hilkiah in the high-priestly line (1 Chronicles 6).
He is called Meshullam in the list of priests who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9).
Ezra's priestly genealogy runs through Shallum son of Zadok (Ezra 7).
Nehemiah lists him as Meshullam among the ancestors of a temple official (Nehemiah 11).

shallum_2520.name: Shallum
shallum_2520.who: A Korahite Levite, son of Kore, who was chief of the gatekeepers at the house of the Lord.
key: Shallum was chief of the gatekeepers stationed at the king's gate on the east (1 Chronicles 9).
He and his Korahite kinsmen guarded the thresholds of the tent (1 Chronicles 9).
His firstborn Mattithiah was in charge of making the flat cakes (1 Chronicles 9).
His descendants were among the gatekeepers who returned from exile (Ezra 2).

shammah_2700.name: Shammah
shammah_2700.who: The third son of Jesse and an older brother of King David.
key: Samuel saw Shammah, but the Lord had not chosen him as king (1 Samuel 16).
He followed Saul to battle against the Philistines with his two older brothers (1 Samuel 17).
His son Jonadab, a very crafty man, advised Amnon in his scheme against Tamar (2 Samuel 13).
Chronicles lists him as Jesse's third son, there called Shimea (1 Chronicles 2).

shedeur_2591.name: Shedeur
shedeur_2591.who: A man of Reuben whose son Elizur led the tribe during Israel's wilderness journey.
key: His son Elizur was named to help Moses take the census for Reuben (Numbers 1).
Elizur son of Shedeur led Reuben's camp on the south side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).
Elizur brought Reuben's offering on the fourth day of the altar's dedication (Numbers 7).
Elizur commanded Reuben's company when Israel set out from Sinai (Numbers 10).

shelumiel_2612.name: Shelumiel
shelumiel_2612.who: The son of Zurishaddai and chief of the tribe of Simeon during the wilderness years.
key: Shelumiel was appointed to help Moses take the census for Simeon (Numbers 1).
He led Simeon's camp on the south side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).
He presented Simeon's offering on the fifth day of the altar's dedication (Numbers 7).
He commanded Simeon's company when Israel set out from Sinai (Numbers 10).

shemaiah_2619.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah_2619.who: A man of God and prophet in Judah during the reign of King Rehoboam.
key: Shemaiah told Rehoboam not to fight against Israel, and the people obeyed (1 Kings 12).
Chronicles repeats this word of the Lord forbidding war with their brothers (2 Chronicles 11).
When Shishak invaded, he told Judah's leaders they had abandoned the Lord (2 Chronicles 12).
After they humbled themselves, he announced God would not destroy them completely (2 Chronicles 12).

sherebiah_2667.name: Sherebiah
sherebiah_2667.who: A Levite of good understanding who returned with Ezra and helped teach the Law to the people.
key: Sherebiah, a man of discretion, joined Ezra's group with his sons and kinsmen (Ezra 8).
Ezra entrusted him with others to carry the silver and gold for the temple (Ezra 8).
He helped the people understand the Law as it was read (Nehemiah 8).
He stood with other Levites leading the people in confession and praise (Nehemiah 9).

shobal_2719.name: Shobal
shobal_2719.who: A son of Seir the Horite and one of the Horite chiefs in the land of Seir.
key: Shobal is listed among the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land (Genesis 36).
His sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam (Genesis 36).
He was one of the chiefs of the Horites in the land of Seir (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats his family line among the descendants of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

sibbechai_2737.name: Sibbecai
sibbechai_2737.who: A Hushathite warrior among David's mighty men who killed a descendant of the giants.
key: Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Saph, a descendant of the giants (2 Samuel 21).
He is listed among the mighty men of David's army (1 Chronicles 11).
Chronicles records that he killed Sippai at Gezer, subduing the Philistines (1 Chronicles 20).
He commanded the division of 24,000 men serving in the eighth month (1 Chronicles 27).

talmon_2820.name: Talmon
talmon_2820.who: A Levite gatekeeper whose family guarded the gates of the house of God before and after the exile.
key: Talmon was among the gatekeepers who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9).
His descendants were among the gatekeepers who returned from Babylon (Ezra 2).
Talmon and his brothers guarded the gates, numbering 172 men (Nehemiah 11).
He was among the gatekeepers guarding the storehouses of the gates (Nehemiah 12).

tirzah_2868.name: Tirzah
tirzah_2868.who: One of the five daughters of Zelophehad of Manasseh, who inherited land because their father had no sons.
key: Tirzah was one of Zelophehad's five daughters, since he had no sons (Numbers 26).
With her sisters she asked Moses for their father's inheritance, and the Lord granted it (Numbers 27).
The sisters married within their father's clan so the inheritance stayed in the tribe (Numbers 36).
They received their inheritance among the clans of Manasseh, as the Lord commanded (Joshua 17).

tychicus_2885.name: Tychicus
tychicus_2885.who: A believer from Asia who traveled with Paul and carried his letters and news to the churches.
key: Tychicus of Asia accompanied Paul on his journey through Macedonia (Acts 20).
Paul sent him, a beloved brother and faithful minister, to share news with the Ephesians (Ephesians 6).
He carried Paul's news to the Colossians, together with Onesimus (Colossians 4).
Paul wrote that he had sent Tychicus to Ephesus (2 Timothy 4).
Paul planned to send Artemas or Tychicus to Titus in Crete (Titus 3).

uri_2895.name: Uri
uri_2895.who: A man of Judah, son of Hur, whose son Bezalel was the chief craftsman of the tabernacle.
key: The Lord called Bezalel son of Uri by name to make the tabernacle (Exodus 31).
Moses announced that God had filled Uri's son Bezalel with skill (Exodus 35).
Bezalel son of Uri made all that the Lord commanded Moses (Exodus 38).
Chronicles lists Uri as son of Hur and father of Bezalel in Judah's line (1 Chronicles 2).
The bronze altar made by Uri's son Bezalel still stood at Gibeon in Solomon's day (2 Chronicles 1).

urijah_2903.name: Uriah
urijah_2903.who: A priest in Jerusalem under King Ahaz who built an altar from a pattern sent from Damascus.
key: Uriah built an altar copied from the model King Ahaz sent from Damascus (2 Kings 16).
At Ahaz's command he offered the regular sacrifices on the new altar (2 Kings 16).
Isaiah took Uriah the priest as a reliable witness to his written prophecy (Isaiah 8).

zebul_3001.name: Zebul
zebul_3001.who: The ruler of the city of Shechem under Abimelech, who exposed Gaal's revolt.
key: Zebul, Abimelech's officer, governed the city of Shechem (Judges 9).
Angered by Gaal's boasting, he secretly sent messengers to warn Abimelech (Judges 9).
He advised Abimelech to lie in wait in the field by night (Judges 9).
He challenged Gaal to fight, then drove Gaal and his relatives out of Shechem (Judges 9).

zedekiah_3029.name: Zedekiah
zedekiah_3029.who: A false prophet, son of Chenaanah, who urged Ahab to battle and struck the prophet Micaiah.
key: Zedekiah made iron horns and prophesied that Ahab would push back the Syrians (1 Kings 22).
He struck Micaiah on the cheek for prophesying disaster (1 Kings 22).
Micaiah said Zedekiah would see the truth when he hid in an inner chamber (1 Kings 22).
Chronicles retells his false prophecy and his striking of Micaiah (2 Chronicles 18).

zerahiah_3047.name: Zerahiah
zerahiah_3047.who: A priest descended from Aaron through Eleazar and Phinehas, listed in the high-priestly genealogy.
key: Chronicles lists Zerahiah son of Uzzi in the line from Aaron to the exile (1 Chronicles 6).
His line continued through his son Meraioth toward Zadok (1 Chronicles 6).
Ezra the scribe traced his own priestly descent through Zerahiah (Ezra 7).

zibeon_3062.name: Zibeon
zibeon_3062.who: A son of Seir the Horite, one of the Horite chiefs, and the grandfather of Esau's wife Oholibamah.
key: Esau's wife Oholibamah was the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon (Genesis 36).
Zibeon is listed among the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land (Genesis 36).
His son Anah found the hot springs while pasturing Zibeon's donkeys (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats his family line among the descendants of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

zuar_3107.name: Zuar
zuar_3107.who: A man of Issachar whose son Nethanel led the tribe during Israel's wilderness journey.
key: His son Nethanel was named to help Moses take the census for Issachar (Numbers 1).
Nethanel son of Zuar led Issachar's camp on the east side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).
Nethanel brought Issachar's offering on the second day of the altar's dedication (Numbers 7).
Nethanel commanded Issachar's company when Israel set out from Sinai (Numbers 10).

zurishaddai_3113.name: Zurishaddai
zurishaddai_3113.who: A man of Simeon whose son Shelumiel led the tribe during Israel's wilderness journey.
key: His son Shelumiel was named to help Moses take the census for Simeon (Numbers 1).
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai led Simeon's camp on the south side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).
Shelumiel brought Simeon's offering on the fifth day of the altar's dedication (Numbers 7).
Shelumiel commanded Simeon's company when Israel set out from Sinai (Numbers 10).
